issues.claim: New Jersey law requires merchants to clearly mark the price of items either on the item or on the display where it is offered for sale (cited to https://www.njconsumeraffairs.gov/News/Brochures/Consumer-Shopping-Guide.pdf).
issues.problem: I read all 24 pages of the cited Consumer Shopping Guide. It contains no price-marking mandate. It covers refund-policy posting, rain checks, layaway, gift cards and scams, and only advises shoppers to 'watch the cash register display to make sure the scanned price matches the advertised or posted price.' The obligation itself appears to exist, but under N.J.S.A. 56:8-2.5 (total selling price 'plainly marked' by stamp, tag, label or sign on the merchandise or where it is offered for sale) - a provision the brief does not cite. As written, a legal rule is presented as confirmed by a source that does not support it.
issues.fix: Re-cite this fact to N.J.S.A. 56:8-2.5 (or the NJ Division of Consumer Affairs release quoting it) and drop the shopping-guide citation for the price-marking requirement. Keep the shopping guide only for what it actually says (e.g. consumers are told to check the register against the posted price).

issues.claim: legal_privacy: 'N.J.A.C. 13:47C-3.5 sets a penalty of not less than $100 per violation, and each package in violation is a separate violation under N.J.S.A. 51:1-100' - presented as the penalty backing the NJ price/tag-accuracy obligation.
issues.problem: The wording is quoted accurately (Cornell LII confirms it), but it is scoped to 'the provisions of this subchapter' - i.e. N.J.A.C. 13:47C Subchapter 3, NONFOODSTUFFS (firewood delivery tickets, holiday decorating materials, building-materials advertising, paper-product quantity declarations). Nothing in that subchapter concerns retail price marking of grocery items, so using 13:47C-3.5 as the price-accuracy penalty misstates the legal basis of the risk the pitch leans on.
issues.fix: State that 13:47C-3.5 covers nonfoodstuffs packaging/quantity rules only, and either drop the $100-per-package figure or source price-marking enforcement from the Consumer Fraud Act route actually used by OWM (the two OAG settlements are the defensible citations).

issues.claim: New Jersey Data Privacy Law thresholds (100,000 NJ consumers, or 25,000 plus data selling; effective Jan 15, 2025), cited to https://lis.njleg.state.nj.us/nxt/gateway.dll/statutes/1/54204/54612.
issues.problem: The cited URL returned HTTP 500 on two attempts, so the source could not be re-opened. The substance checks out against P.L. 2023, c.266 (S332): 100,000 consumers, or 25,000 plus revenue/discount from selling personal data, effective Jan 15, 2025.
issues.fix: Replace the dead statute link with https://pub.njleg.gov/Bills/2022/PL23/266_.HTM (P.L. 2023, c.266) or the DCA NJDPA FAQ page.

issues.claim: State v. Diaz (1998) held the video portion of a recording is outside the NJ Wiretap Act, cited to https://caselaw.findlaw.com/court/nj-superior-court-appellate-division/1193224.html.
issues.problem: That URL returned HTTP 403, so the cited page could not be re-opened by a verifier. The holding and year are correct (308 N.J. Super. 504 (App. Div. 1998): video portion outside the Act; audio portion separately upheld under the consent provision).
issues.fix: Swap in an openable citation (e.g. a court-opinion PDF or openjurist record for 308 N.J. Super. 504) so the claim can be checked without a paywall/block.

issues.claim: Zippedi pricing: 'no published price; a distributor listing describes acquisition via written quote or robot-as-a-service (robot-distribution.com/en/brands/zippedi)'.
issues.problem: The source_url given is home.zippedi.com/zippy/, which I opened and which says nothing about purchasing or pricing. The distributor listing is named inline but is not the cited URL and I did not open it, so the 'quote or RaaS' description is unverified.
issues.fix: Either add the robot-distribution.com URL as an explicit source and open it, or reduce the entry to 'Unknown - no published price'.

issues.claim: Reolink hardware: 'the full category also includes cheaper non-4K and refurbished units and models up to $899'.
issues.problem: I confirmed page 1 of 4 of the cited 4K PoE category (list $79.99-$199.99, current $47.99-$119.99), but not the claimed $899 top end or the presence of non-4K/refurbished units - the category listing is paginated (30 results) and the cited page shows only nine.

issues.problem: These footprint, aisle and staffing ranges have no source and, unlike the other four buyer entries, are not marked as inference. Only the 186-establishment count is sourced (BLS QCEW 2024).
issues.fix: Add '(inference)' to the size range, as the other buyer entries do.

issues.problem: Sub-scores do add to the total (13+10+8+13+11+6 = 61), so the arithmetic is sound. But 11 is generous for a section that itself lists two unconfirmed items (employee-notice duty, NJ retention limit), one pending bill (A3929) and - after correction - an unresolved price-marking penalty basis.
